grain.value: One row per application in the authenticated user's Licensing To Do queue, identified by the application entity key; the public row reference is the Application No.

population.value: The complete pending To Do queue returned by the personal My Application Tasks operation under its exact request context; it includes pending modification and external approval as well as pending review.

filterScope.value: No user-entered narrowing filter; the queue is bound to the authenticated account and the endpoint's runtime approval department.

caveats.value: This queue shows work routed to your account, not all Licensing work in the department; a Manager role does not turn it into a team queue.
The To Do summary counters are a separate count source and are not proof of the list's completeness.

knowledgeRequirementCoverage.reason: The To Do read contract defines the row entity: id identifies the application entity, and applicationNumber is the public row reference in the Application No. column; page-scoped aliases explicitly exclude licence entities and workflow tasks. requiredPoints: The list rows are Licensing applications (submitted service requests), not licenses or generic workflow tasks.
Each row is identified publicly by its Application No. (applicationNumber).

knowledgeRequirementCoverage.reason: Application grain is id; the personal To Do projection deduplicates by (id, dispositionCaseId), and a single application can carry multiple taskIds over time, so projected task rows are a different unit. The completed contract states the same grain rule, so no internal contradiction.
requiredPoints: The list is at application grain: each distinct application is identified by its entity key, not by workflow task rows.
A single application can have multiple task IDs over time, so task rows are not the same unit as applications.

knowledgeRequirementCoverage.reason: Personal scope is defined as the authenticated user task list filtered by the endpoint runtime approval department, with no user-entered narrowing filter; the manual confirms personal scope under current Applications page permission and active To Do tab. The Manager-role clause is consistent, not opposing.
requiredPoints: The queue is personal: it shows tasks from the authenticated user's task list, not the whole department or team.
A Manager role does not turn this personal queue into a team queue.
The list is filtered by the endpoint's runtime approval department.

requiredPoints: The To Do view is the pending-work queue on the Licensing applications page, selected by the To Do tab.

The To Do summary card is a count, not the list itself.
